title: Post-October review and remediation index

countingPolicy.findingCount: Only individually adjudicated records in the 2026-11-10 review are counted as 34 findings; the 2026-11-12 follow-up adds W7 and W8.
countingPolicy.commentCount: CodeRabbit review comments, review submissions and threads are signals, not defect counts.
countingPolicy.duplicatePolicy: Repeated review comments or repeated scans are not new findings unless the triggering invariant or root cause is materially distinct.
countingPolicy.statusPolicy: fixed-main means the fix commit is an ancestor of main@445f421d; fix-in-flight means an open repair PR exists; open means no linked repair was verified; suspected remains unconfirmed.

sources.interpretation: Five exports 35+46+41+54+29. Fingerprint reconciliation is required; not 205 unique defects.
Workflow failures are not bug counts.
Five merge-resolution findings, four verified main-line defects, one additional non-reproducible observation; remaining comments are review observations, not automatically accepted bugs.
Snapshot of review activity; comments require adjudication and deduplication.
W7 fixed by #813; W8 has an operational workaround but no structural repair verified.

findings.summary: Delivery fee entered seller settlement and commission base, carrier payable was missing, and order-leg completion lacked the formal payment-intent binding.
Full refund reversed seller credit but not the commission mirror, leaving seller balance negative by the commission.
Concurrent delivery refund-delta read/modify/write could overbook cumulative refund totals.
Retryable refund work ran inside a REQUIRED carrier transaction and could poison the caller after an external PSP effect.
Refunding a fulfilled but never-paid order was rejected, leaving the return stuck in RECEIVED.
Role-revoke endpoint could remove the last active ADMIN; #818 is merged and its merge commit is reachable from main.
A disabled account could perform irreversible self-service deletion while an access token remained valid.
Provider-eligibility law could not be reached by a team member without PROVIDER role; claim-approval ownership handoff did not grant the required role.
Administrative decision engines and review-queue reads may lack the service-layer third gate; the original report marks this suspected.
Community purge statements did not advance optimistic versions, allowing stale writes to race erasure; #817 is merged and reachable from main.
Messaging purge did not advance the row version, permitting stale inbox transitions to conflict with erased PII.
Account erasure left media rows UPLOADED and S3 objects available to signed-URL read surfaces.
Notifications purge did not advance lock versions and had no adapter test; #824 adds real-PostgreSQL proof and remains open.
findings.evidenceNote: The code/version-advance adapter fix and an initial adapter test are on main through #817; stronger real-PostgreSQL/Testcontainers proof remains open in #824, so the concurrency-evidence follow-up is not closed.

findings.summary: Jobs purge advanced the application version but not the authored job text version.
Catalog listing/Q&A purge omitted optimistic-version advancement on relevant authored rows.
Knowledge tombstone filtering may not cover all public board/search/detail read rails; the original report marks this suspected.
GraphQL exception mapping discarded the shared ApiProblemDetail taxonomy and exposed inconsistent error codes compared with REST.
PaymentStateChangedEvent used free-form states with divergent vocabularies; listeners could silently ignore events.
Favorites REST endpoint returned a raw Page while the rest of the API returned PagedResponse.
Enum/type-mismatch request failures returned 500 instead of the documented 400 VAL-001 response.
Money had inconsistent GraphQL representations (Float versus String minor units) in the same schema.
Geographic autocomplete silently truncated results at 20 with no has-more indicator.
Unified search silently discarded a sort parameter that the sibling surface validated or rejected.
REST errors carried traceId while GraphQL errors omitted it by default.
Webhook deduplication test did not exercise the V42 unique-index serialization path on the real migration schema.
Terminal-state test asserted one forbidden edge while claiming to prove that all terminal states reject every outgoing transition.
Vertex-mode test was skipped by assumeTrue in CI because the required ADC environment was absent.
Booking-scope integration test could pass with an empty database and therefore did not prove that the correct booking's dispute was selected.
Aggregate production health was DOWN due to SMTP contribution and repeated public-endpoint probe failures; owner decision is required for SMTP policy.
Deployable profiles inherited localhost as the identity-mail link origin, causing password-reset and verification links to point to localhost.
Missing PSP channel silently entered a local inert consumer-money path rather than failing with 503 SU-001.
Governance docs on main claimed gate-health.yml was present although that workflow existed only on the commerce candidate at the audit head.
Versioned Railway target record drifted from the live deployment-variable inventory; CI cannot query provider truth.
Staging AI/RAG configuration diverged from production despite a documented staging-is-production-like contract.
OpenRewrite invoked system Maven 3.9.15 while the project enforcer required Maven >=3.10; #813 switched to the pinned wrapper and the fix is on main.
CodeRabbit Gate poll accepted an empty-body approval while exact processed-file coverage rejected the same review, creating a deadlock after threads were resolved.

separateHistoricalCases.summary: Order/delivery row locks were acquired in opposite order on concurrent paths, creating an ABBA deadlock window.
OSRM route lookup performed outbound HTTP while a database transaction and order row lock were held.
The review poll and the exact-file evidence verifier used incompatible acceptance rules for an empty-body CodeRabbit approval.
OpenRewrite used an unpinned Maven executable and failed against the repository's Maven Enforcer floor; #813 now uses the Maven Wrapper.
The purge version-advance change had only weak structural proof until a real PostgreSQL/Testcontainers test proved stale writes fail and replay remains idempotent.
The OpenRewrite catalog job ran on Dependabot PRs and converted a supported automated dependency update into a persistent CI failure requiring manual intervention.
Nine vendored Neon skills existed without a reviewed pin/provenance registry; the merged change introduced a reviewed pinned skills surface.

capabilityAndDecisionGaps.summary: Discount/voucher semantics are not fully proven: manual discount precedence, voucher suppression/restoration, shipping-voucher exceptions and manual line discounts.
Order discount mutations and Saleor-style proportional discount allocation are not implemented/proven; currency quantization and remainder behavior remain gaps.
Catalog/inventory/stock/warehouse semantic coverage requires a dedicated audit.
Gift-card liability ownership and full lifecycle require owner-approved D-GC-001 decisions.
Tax-class and configuration behavior is split between NOT_STARTED and BLOCKED_BY_DECISION under D-TAX-001.
Commerce-channel ownership and cross-domain context need D-CHANNEL-001.
Shop/refund/return settings ownership needs D-SHOP-001 and D-SETTINGS-001.

limitations: The 75 PR entries created after #746 were inventoried from GitHub PR metadata and available descriptions; detailed diffs/review evidence were concentrated on PRs that report or carry defects, remediations, review shards, or governance changes. Dependency/OpenRewrite-only PRs were classified by their purpose and description, not treated as defect findings.

The 682 CodeRabbit comments on #806–#811 are individual review comments with distinct comment fingerprints in that snapshot, not 682 confirmed unique defects. A single finding can generate multiple comments/review iterations; some comments are test-shard artifacts, nits, false positives, or repeated observations.
The review finding registry is a reconciliation index for the named reports. It does not claim a complete historical diff audit of every commit in all 75 PRs.
